paper_title: DIY-MKG An LLM-Based Polyglot Language Learning System
caption: DIY-MKG reliably expands the vocabulary with low sensitivity to the language and the starting word. For each language, 10 opaque curves represent vocabulary sizes obtained from 10 different starting words, and one solid curve represents the average of the 10 curves. The standard deviations across languages and starting words are small, indicating fairness for all language learners. The diagonal gray line represents the upper-bound of vocabulary size, assuming all words in each iteration have not yet appeared in the vocabulary. While the real expansion rate is lower, the vocabulary does not saturate after 500 iterations. Therefore, DIY-MKG can reliably help the language learner to expand their vocabulary by consistently introducing new words.
model_annotation: The plot illustrates vocabulary size as a function of the number of iterations for three languages: Spanish, Korean, and Japanese. The x-axis is labeled "Number of Iterations" and uses a linear scale ranging from 0 to 500, with tick labels at 0, 100, 200, 300, 400, and 500. The y-axis is labeled "Vocabulary Size" and employs a linear scale from 0 to 5000. A gray diagonal line is present, starting at (0, 0) and ending at (500, 5000). The Spanish line is blue and solid, starting at (0, 100) and ending at (500, 4800), with a generally increasing trend. The Korean line is orange with a dashed line style and markers, starting at (0, 160) and ending at (500, 4500), demonstrating an increasing trend. The Japanese line is green with a dashed line style and markers, beginning at (0, 160) and terminating at (500, 4500), also exhibiting an increasing trend.
